references.text: The Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord when I stretch out my hand against Egypt - the same theme of God revealing himself through his acts toward Egypt.
Parallel text in the same chapter where God says he will glorify himself through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians shall know that he is the Lord.
The immediately preceding verse which mentions that God will glorify himself through Pharaoh, his chariots, and his horsemen.
Ezekiel uses the same expression 'they shall know that I am the Lord' when God glorifies himself through judgment.
Prophecy against Egypt where God says the Egyptians shall know that he is the Lord - an echo of the deliverance from Egypt.
Another prophecy against Egypt with the formula 'they shall know that I am the Lord,' linking back to the Exodus narrative.
The psalmist praises God who saved the Israelites for his name's sake, to make known his power - reflecting on the events in Exodus 14.
Paul quotes concerning Pharaoh and explains that God raised him up to show his power and so that his name might be proclaimed throughout the earth.
Thematic parallel: Judgment against Egypt as a means to reveal God's identity, even though the historical context and timing differ.
Allusive connection: Ezekiel uses language from the Exodus (fire and crushing) to describe a future judgment against Egypt.
Complementary relationship: The source verse explains the mechanism (judgment on Pharaoh) to achieve the goal mentioned in this verse (knowledge of God).
Whole and part: The source verse is the concrete moment when the goal mentioned in this verse (to know God) is fully realized.
